newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss report three new cases of mad cow disease.
newsitem.headline: Swiss report three new cases of mad cow disease.

text.p: Swiss federal veterinary authorities reported three new cases of Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE) on Friday.

The latest report brought the number of BSE cases in Switzerland to 230 in total. This was second only to Britain, but still running far behind the number of cases reported there -- expected to be about 8,000 this year.
For this year alone, Swiss authorities have reported 45 cows with the disease.
BSE, commonly known as "mad cow" disease, is a suspected transmitter of a type of the brain-wasting Creuzfeldt-Jakob Disease (CJD) which affects humans.

All three new cases were reported in the canton of Graubunden, but from different farms. One of the afflicted cows was born after 1990, the date when Switzerland forbade feeding animal meal to cows. Switzerland banned the import of potentially contaminated animal meal in 1988, but allowed farmers to use existing feed stocks until 1990.
The Swiss government has recommended slaughtering 230,000 cows to restore confidence in the country's beef industry.

To date, no known cases of the type of CJD linked to mad cow disease have been reported in Switzerland, but beef consumption in the country has dropped and some countries also have refused to import Swiss beef.
